correctness.rationale: Convexity of every squared-norm summand on the product of square unit balls permits a maximizer at product extreme points \((\pm1,\pm1)\), all of which lie on the sphere. Introducing a global auxiliary sign converts the original half-cube average to a full Rademacher average. For a sign pattern with \(k\) equal coordinate parities, the two coordinate sums are \(A+B\) and \(A-B\); the identity \(\max\{(A+B)^2,(A-B)^2\}=A^2+B^2+2|AB|\), plus independence, gives exactly \(1+(2/n)a_ka_{n-k}\). The parity maximization follows from \(a_{2q-1}=a_{2q}\) and the strict log-concavity ratio \(c_{q+1}/c_q=(2q+1)/(2q)\); Stirling gives the limit. An independent exact enumeration over all vertex sign patterns through \(n=8\) reproduced values \(2,5/3,7/4,8/5,7/4,23/14,109/64\).

value.rationale: The square plane is the canonical two-dimensional non-Hilbert \(\ell_\infty\) space, and the result fills exactly the fixed-dimension regime excluded from the existing high-dimensional formula. The all-n formula and its finite non-Hilbert limit give a natural benchmark for how modified n-th constants behave when dimension does not grow with n.
residual_risks: No classification of all maximizing tuples is supplied.

final_claim: For the real square plane \(\ell_\infty^2\), the upper modified \(n\)-th von Neumann--Jordan constant is \(1+(2/n)\max_{0\le k\le n}a_ka_{n-k}\), with the stated parity formulas and limit \(1+2/\pi\), where \(a_r\) is the mean absolute displacement of an \(r\)-step simple random walk.
limitations: Only the upper modified constant is evaluated; no claim is made for unmodified or lower constants.
